key_insight: RuO2 behaves as a moderately correlated Fermi liquid, and DFT+DMFT captures its charge transport well while revealing a significant mismatch in thermal transport.
engineering_relevance: The work provides a precision benchmark for predicting electrical, thermoelectric, and thermal transport in complex oxides relevant to electronic and thermal device design.
method: Realistic dynamical mean-field theory (DFT+DMFT) in the paramagnetic state
Computed spectroscopic and transport observables: optical conductivity, resistivity, thermopower, and thermal resistivity
Compared theory against complementary experiments to test Fermi-liquid behavior
evidence_signal: The calculations show semi-quantitative agreement with experiment for optical conductivity, electrical resistivity, and thermopower, but substantially underestimate the low-temperature thermal resistivity.
watch_item: A remaining discrepancy in electronic thermal resistivity suggests missing physics—possibly low-temperature electron-phonon scattering—and the full charge/heat relaxation picture is not yet resolved.
paper_title: Unraveling Fermi liquid charge and heat transport in RuO$_{2}$
